```{r}
#| label: "GEE_Plumes"
#| fig-cap: "Figure1. Surface Turbidity Trends Across Reef Locations. Higher values indicate more suspended sediment and organic matter near the sea surface, while lower values indicate clearer oceanic water"

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)

# 1. Read data & clean station labels
#Extracted satellite turbidity proxy values from Google Earth Engine

gee_s3 <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "Burdekin_S3_Plume_TimeSeries.csv")) %>%
  mutate(
    date = ymd(date),
    station = factor(station,
      levels = c("S1_Burdekin_Mouth", "S2_Magnetic_Island", "S3_Davies_Reef"),
      labels = c("Burdekin Mouth", "Magnetic Island", "Davies Reef")
    )
  )

# 2. Plot smooth trend per location
plot <- ggplot(gee_s3, aes(x = date, y = s3_turbidity_ratio, color = station, fill = station)) +
  geom_smooth(span = 0.6, linewidth = 1.3, alpha = 0.18) +
  facet_wrap(~ station) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#009E73"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#009E73"), guide = "none") +
    labs(
      x = "Wet Season (2023 - 2024)",
      y = "Satellite Turbidity Proxy",
      caption = "Figure 1. Surface Turbidity Trends Across Reef Locations. Higher values indicate more suspended sediment and organic matter near the sea surface, while lower values indicate clearer oceanic water."
  )+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)+
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 10, color = "#444444"),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing    = unit(1.5, "lines")
  )


print(plot)
ggsave(here("outputs", "figures", "Flood_Plumes.png"), plot, width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 300)

```

```{r}
#| label: "Flood_Plume"
#| fig-cap: "Figure2. Burdekin River Runoff & Post-Flood Dissipation Timeline (WMIP Station 120006B). Dashed green line = dry-season Q90 baseline (5,248 ML/day); shaded orange window = 81-day active flood tail."

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)

# 1. Load & filter QLD WMIP discharge telemetry (Station 120006B: Burdekin at Clare)
burdekin_ts <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "burdekin.csv"),
  skip = 4,
  col_names = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(str_detect(X1, "^\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}")) %>%
  transmute(
    date             = as.Date(X1, format = "%H:%M:%S %d/%m/%Y"),
    runoff_ML_day = as.numeric(X14),
    runoff_qual   = as.numeric(X15)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(date), runoff_qual <= 130)

# 2. Compute dry-season baseline (Nov-Dec Q90), peak flow, & 81-day recovery date
baseline_q90 <- burdekin_ts %>%
  filter(month(date) %in% c(11, 12)) %>%
  summarise(q90 = quantile(runoff_ML_day, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(q90)

peak_row      <- burdekin_ts %>% slice_max(runoff_ML_day, n = 1)
peak_date     <- peak_row$date
peak_flow     <- peak_row$runoff_ML_day

recovery_date <- burdekin_ts %>%
  filter(date > peak_date, runoff_ML_day <= baseline_q90) %>%
  slice_min(date, n = 1) %>%
  pull(date)

dissipation_days <- as.numeric(recovery_date - peak_date)

# Exponential decay half-life (Peak -> Recovery)
vis_fit <- burdekin_ts %>%
  filter(date >= peak_date, date <= recovery_date) %>%
  mutate(days_since_peak = as.numeric(date - peak_date)) %>%
  lm(log(runoff_ML_day) ~ days_since_peak, data = .)

clarity <- round(-log(2) / coef(vis_fit)[["days_since_peak"]], 1) #half-life 

# 3. Build clean single-panel Figure 1 (Discharge hydrograph only)
burdekin_fp <- ggplot(burdekin_ts, aes(x = date, y = runoff_ML_day / 1000)) +
  # Shaded 81-day active flood window
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = ymd("2024-01-25"), xmax = recovery_date,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.10
  ) +
  # Discharge area & line
  geom_area(fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(color = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1.2) +
  # Dry-season Q90 baseline dashed line
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = baseline_q90 / 1000,
    linetype = "dashed", color = "#009E73", linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  # Peak flow marker & arrow callout
  geom_point(data = peak_row, aes(x = date, y = runoff_ML_day / 1000), color = "#D55E00", size = 3) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = ymd("2023-12-08"), y = 132, hjust = 0, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", color = "#111111",
    label = "Peak Flow: 212,272 ML/day\n(4 Feb 2024)"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "segment",
    x = ymd("2024-01-08"), y = 148, xend = peak_date - days(2), yend = (peak_flow / 1000) - 3,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), color = "#222222", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  # Dissipation metrics summary box in top-right
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = ymd("2024-04-29"), y = 215, hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
    size = 3.4, fontface = "bold", color = "#D55E00", fill = "white", alpha = 0.92,
    label = paste0(
      "Total Dissipation: ", dissipation_days, " days\n",
      "Flood Plume Half-Life (t½): ", clarity, " days\n",
      "Baseline Return: 25 Apr 2024"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(ymd("2023-11-01"), ymd("2024-05-01"), by = "1 month"),
    date_labels = "%b"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 230)) +
  labs(
    x = "Wet Season (2023–2024)",
    y = "Riverine Runoff (1000ml/day)", 
    caption = "Figure2. Burdekin River Runoff & Post-Flood Dissipation Timeline (WMIP Station 120006B). Dashed green line = dry-season Q90 baseline (5,248 ML/day); shaded orange window = 81-day active flood tail."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12.5),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "#444444"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(burdekin_fp)

ggsave(
  filename = here("outputs", "figures", "Burdekin_Runoff.png"),
  plot     = burdekin_fp,
  width    = 11,
  height   = 4.4,
  dpi      = 300
)

```
